market_name: Will 5 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check 2y/10y Treasury yields and fed funds futures (SOFR/SR3) for a confirming dovish shift; confirm the Polymarket probability move is real and not thin-book noise.
time_plan.1h: Re-check whether yields are sustaining the move or mean-reverting; scan for any Fed-speak or data release that could be the actual driver.
time_plan.2h: Compare TLT move vs rate-futures-implied move to see if ETF is lagging or leading; watch for reversal.
time_plan.6h: Assess whether the dovish repricing held through a US session; check for FOMC commentary or inflation prints.
time_plan.12h: Final check: did TLT net move in the dovish direction, and did the prediction-market shift precede or follow public rate moves?

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 5 Fed cuts in 2026 signals a more dovish rate path than currently priced. Lower expected policy rates pull the whole Treasury curve lower in yield, lifting bond prices. TLT is the most duration-sensitive liquid proxy, so a dovish repricing would push it up. The link is direct and mechanical, but 2026 cut expectations are a slow-moving macro variable, so a 12h move is modest and easily swamped by other macro data.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and EURUSD for confirming dollar weakness alongside the dovish rate move.
time_plan.1h: See if dollar move tracks the rate-differential story or is being driven by non-US factors (ECB, BoJ, risk sentiment).
time_plan.2h: Evaluate whether dollar weakness persists or reverses; check correlation with TLT move for internal consistency.
time_plan.6h: Reassess across the US session; watch for data surprises that override the Fed-path signal.
time_plan.12h: Final check: net dollar direction and whether the prediction-market move had any leading information content.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrows US rate differentials versus other G10 economies, which is typically dollar-negative. UUP tracks the broad dollar and would soften on a dovish repricing. The channel is real but second-order relative to bonds, and FX also depends on what other central banks are expected to do, so the signal is weaker and noisier over 12h.

evidence_used: Market question on number of 2026 Fed 25bp cuts; a shift toward 5 cuts implies a more dovish policy path
Standard macro transmission: dovish rate expectations lower Treasury yields and weaken the dollar
TLT and UUP are highly liquid, broadly-traded proxies for duration and the dollar
uncertainty_notes: 2026 cut expectations are slow-moving; a 12h window captures little of the thesis
The 700bps tradable threshold is far above any plausible 12h move in these macro proxies
Prediction-market probability moves on this question may reflect noise/thin liquidity rather than new information
Mislabeled primary topic (military_conflict) suggests metadata is unreliable

llm_justification.summary: This market prices how dovish the 2026 Fed path will be. A sharp rise in the probability of 5 cuts is a dovish signal that mechanically favors lower Treasury yields (TLT up) and a softer dollar (UUP down). Both links are directionally sound but second-order over a 12h horizon, with modest expected magnitudes far below the 700bps tradable bar, so neither is tradable and confidence is moderate at best.
key_assumptions: A probability shift toward more cuts reflects a genuinely more dovish rate path, not noise
Rate differentials and duration transmission channels operate normally
No offsetting shocks (risk-off, other central banks, inflation surprise) dominate the 12h window
failure_modes: The dovish repricing is already public (reacting to data/Fed-speak), so no leading edge exists
Prediction-market move is thin-book noise with no information content
Over 12h, idiosyncratic macro flows swamp the Fed-path signal, reversing the expected direction
Dollar move is driven by foreign central-bank expectations, breaking the clean US-rate link
Expected magnitudes are tiny vs the 700bps threshold, so even a correct direction is non-tradable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
